name: Judaism
description: an ancient, monotheistic religion and way of life for the Jewish people, centered on a covenant with one God, revealed through the Torah (Hebrew Bible) and traditions, emphasizing ethical conduct, community, and holiness in daily life, making it a foundational faith for Christianity and Islam.

branches.name: Orthodox Judaism
branches.description: advocates a strict observance of Jewish law, or halakha, which is to be interpreted and determined only according to traditional methods and in adherence to the continuum of received precedent through the ages.

branches.name: Conservative Judaism
branches.description: a Jewish religious movement that regards the authority of Jewish law and tradition as emanating primarily from the assent of the people through the generations, more than from divine revelation. It therefore views Jewish law, or Halakha, as both binding and subject to historical development.

branches.name: Reform Judaism
branches.description: a major Jewish denomination that emphasizes the evolving nature of Judaism, the superiority of its ethical aspects to its ceremonial ones, and belief in a continuous revelation which is closely intertwined with human reason and not limited to the theophany at Mount Sinai.
